newsitem.title: UK: Britain launches new commercial payments standard.
newsitem.headline: Britain launches new commercial payments standard.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and the British Standards Institution on Tuesday launched a new set of rules aimed at tackling the problem of late payment of commercial debt.

A CBI statement said the new standard, called BS7890, departed from existing codes of practice by providing guidelines for sellers as well as buyers. It would become legally binding only if both parties entered into a contract to supply goods or services quoting the Standard as a means of transaction.
"We urge all businesses to embrace this standard," CBI director general Adair Turner said.

"The CBI is very concerned about the problems caused by the late payment of commercial debt, particularly for smaller firms," he said. The new standard supplements an existing CBI Prompt Payment Code with over 1,000 UK signatories, he said.
Treasury Secretary Angela Knight said the Treasury supported the new standard and had signed up to paying all properly made up bills within 30 days unless stated otherwise in the contract.
"This should help ensure that we get a better performance from which small firms in particular will benefit," she said.
